title: Surface per-tenant tail latency, KV-hit-zone heatmaps, and trace-context propagation to eliminate console darkspots from capacity regressions
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Summary: During the 2026-02-25 capacity regression (INC-2026-02-25-GPU-BURST) we observed a large number of customer-facing tail-latency spikes that were not visible in existing console dashboards. Dashboards showed stable median latencies and aggregate GPU utilization, but several customers experienced degraded throughput and repeated fallback to lower-capacity model variants. Postmortem identified three blind spots: (1) no per-tenant 99/99.9th tail latency series, (2) KV cache hit metrics were global only and did not expose partition/zone skew, and (3) trace-context was dropped across async job boundaries (batching workers / offloaded pre-tokenization) making end-to-end request attribution impossible.

Impact: High — multiple enterprise customers experienced elevated latency and throttle escalations for ~2 hours during peak. Because console lacked per-tenant tails and KV-hit partitioning, incident detection and targeted mitigation took longer and we executed a broad capacity scale-up instead of precise routing fixes.

Root cause analysis:
- Monitoring: existing metrics aggregated by service and model-class hide per-tenant hot tails. Rules and alerts are defined on medians/p50 or p95 which missed minority but high-impact tenants.
- KV cache telemetry: instrumentation emitted only global hits and evictions; the runtime sharded KV caches per-GPU and by tenant affinity. Skewed load to a small set of shards led to local cache thrashing without global signals.
- Tracing: async handoffs to batch workers strip traceparent headers for internal jobs; sampled traces stop at the request-router boundary, so we can't correlate inflight GPU queue time to originating customer requests.

Proposed action items (owners & estimates):
1) Add per-tenant tail latency metrics (p99, p99.9) and expose them as per-route and per-model time series. Owner: Jin Park (ENG). Estimate: 3 pts.
2) Emit KV-cache metrics partitioned by shard/gpu and tenant affinity (hit%, eviction rate, avg TTL). Owner: Ravi Shah (ENG). Estimate: 3 pts.
3) Create a KV-hit heatmap dashboard showing GPU shard vs tenant dense-slice to catch skewed hotspots. Owner: Product Analytics (PM) + Design for visualization. Estimate: 2 pts.
4) Fix trace propagation across async batch jobs: ensure traceparent preserved in task payloads and add tracing hooks in batch worker startup. Owner: Aisha Patel (Infra). Estimate: 2 pts.
5) Add alerting rules that trigger on small-population tail events (detect p99 spikes affecting >=1% of tenants or absolute-response > X ms). Owner: SRE (Tom Chen). Estimate: 1 pt.
6) Run a synthetic tenant-skew chaos test to validate heatmap and alerting. Owner: Reliability Eng. Estimate: 2 pts.

Acceptance criteria:
- New p99/p99.9 time series available in console for each tenant and route, with at least 15m resolution and 48h retention.
- KV cache shard-level hit/eviction metrics emitted and visualized in a dashboard with filters for tenant and GPU shard.
- End-to-end traces consistently show request-router -> batch-worker -> gpu-exec spans for >95% of sampled traces during a synthetic test.
- New alerting rules validated by the chaos test and onboarded to PagerDuty runbook.

Risks & notes:
- Per-tenant high-cardinality metrics increase cardinality; plan includes cardinality controls (ingest sampling, rollup tiers, and retention policies).
- Tracing fixes add small payload overhead on async tasks; evaluate sampling rate adjustments to limit load.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident: INC-2026-02-25-GPU-BURST (internal link)
- Postmortem doc: drive.redwood/pm/postmortems/2026-02-25-capacity-regression (link)
- Initial dashboard mockup: drive.redwood/design/kv-heatmap-mock.png
- Design spec: drive.redwood/design/console-tail-metrics-spec.md

Follow-ups: schedule a retro with SRE + PM + Product Analytics two weeks after rollout to verify operational overhead and false positive rate of new alerts.
